utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Morrissey, you have something to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Your Honour, I asked that the Court come in before the witness because of the matters that were raised yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We're -- I don't think we're in private session. Is my learned friend going --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We are now in the open session. Well, there's two things I would like to mention at this stage. The first one is that concerning with Friday's schedule, since the Judges will have an extraordinary Plenary in the afternoon, so we could only sit in the morning, so we'll start from 9.00 until 12.30 with 30 minutes' break in between. The next issue is about the response from the Prosecution to the Defence request for tender some documents through the last week's witness. I understand it will take some time for the Prosecution team to study all those documents tendered by the Defence, but I hope the Prosecution's team could submit their views on those documents as early as possible, since we have to make a decision, and there's still a possibility for the application for certification from the Defence team. Yes. I think that -- could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could we briefly move to the private session, Your Honour, because of a matter I wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Morrissey: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm just indicate, Witness F, what remains for you today by way of the topics to question you about. I have some more questions and a couple of documents to show you concerning the events of July of 1993, and then I'm going to move to the Trebevic -- Trebevic operation, focussing chiefly on October of 1993 but with a couple of questions about September. And I'm going to show you some documents from that era as well. Some of those documents you may recall; some of them you may not. And you must feel free to comment on that as I put them to you one after another. But you may take as much time to look at those documents as you need. Now, my first question concerns the -- the incidents of the 1st and the 2nd -- sorry, of the 2nd and the 3rd of July of 1993, which you've already given evidence about. I wish to ask you a couple of questions about that. First of all, do you recall the name of the man who had the nickname Talijan, the proper name of that man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his proper name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Talijan's real name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mustafa Hajrulahovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time of the incident on the 2nd and 3rd of July, was he the commander of the 1st Corps of the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what I want to do now is to show you a document purporting to come from him. There are some attached documents to it as well. But this document is a document dated 1st of July, 1993. So it's a document coming from just before the incident. And I'll have some questions for you about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown -- it's 65 ter number D146. Its ERN number will be DD000643, and it's to be MFI255.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document will appear on the screen in just a moment in the Bosnian format, but what it appears to be is a -- an official note from Mustafa Hajrulahovic, Talijan, to the SVK command -- commander, in fact. And what I want to ask you about is, first of all, to look at the document and ask you some questions about the document. And then if you don't know the document, I'll ask you some questions more generally about it. Do you have that document in front of you yet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thanks. Now, first of all, does that appear to be a -- a document signed and stamped under the name of Mustafa Hajrulahovic, Talijan, and dated the 1st of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This was not signed by Mustafa Hajrulahovic, known as Talijan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is -- whose is -- are you able to say whose the signature is under that name on the Bosnian original?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was issued by the security service of the 1st Corps, and it is signed by Chief Sacir Arnautovic, who was then the official chief. But this is not his signature, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you looking at a document --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just -- there may be some confusion between the English one and the Bosnian original that you have. Just could you just describe -- the document that you're looking at, is that a document dated the 1st of July with a document number above it 02/1109-1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that's not it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Your Honours, we may have a technical hitch here. Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Prosecutor, and -- and Witness F, the document has a number of parts to it, and it may be now that the witness is being shown one part in Bosnian. Could the witness please be shown page 2 of the Bosnian version but keep with page 1 of the -- of the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While that's being brought up, I indicate I'm really showing you this document to see if you can comment on the situation that existed immediately before that incident of the 2nd of July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see the document. This document was signed by Mustafa Hajrulahovic, and this document is in fact an attachment to the document we saw just a minute ago which arrived from the security services. I haven't read this through all the way, but it's probably the opinion of the commander of the 1st Corps, Mustafa Hajrulahovic, about the attitude of his subordinates towards him and towards their tasks. I was not involved in this, so I am not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that -- that's my next question. Is this -- first of all, is that a document which you yourself have actually seen before today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Bearing in mind -- all right. I'm going to ask you to look at the -- at the second document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the first page of the Bosnian version, but it will be the third page of the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Is that the document you -- you looked at before to which the Talijan statement is annexed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't seen this document before either. These are documents that circulated within the security services, but I myself have not seen them before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated yesterday that sometimes you would attend the meetings of the security services and that sometimes you would see that senior people had documents with them. Now, let me ask you: In broad terms, were you familiar with the -- the problems that the commander of the 1st Corps thought that he had with the 10th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, I attended a meeting of the security services within the security service administration, but I did not go to any external meetings. The meetings I attended were morning briefings. And in such situations, the superior commander -- my superior commander, that is, in most cases simply summarised the problems and told us about the problems generally. He didn't go into details. The exception was when there was an issue that somebody was working with. Then they would be shown the documents to see so that they could continue being involved in this situation and monitoring it. As for the other part of your question, in principle I was aware that Musan Topalovic was behaving in an opportunistic manner in connection with orders issued by the commander of the 1st Corps, so I was informed of this situation in a general way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I offer that document for tender, noting that this witness has indicated very clearly that he himself didn't see it. Perhaps before I offer it, I just want to ask one more question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the face of it and having regard only to formal matters, does it appear to be a -- a normal communication within the SVB, or a regular form of communication within the SVB?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is that a question to me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This manner of communication was usual in the security service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apart from this, there was certain information passed on, but this was simply a document with an attachment. Official notes from subordinate units could reach us at the level of the security service administration only if the matter was very important and if the information had been verified so that we could see the authentic document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And is this one document or two documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's one document. It's a note -- the official document, I think, is the -- the document which has just been shown -- that part of the document which has just been shown, the note under the name of Sacir Arnautovic, which is currently in its English version on the screen. Attached to that are a number of other documents, so -- some of which I'm not going to cross-examine about because they're -- they form part of the document, so I'm not going to edit them out, but they -- I don't need this witness's evidence about them. But it consists of that document that's in -- the official note, which you have in front of you, plus the attachments which were attached to it. And it should form just one document, because that's the way we got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: With the number of 255?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next I want to move to what was happening during the events of the 2nd and 3rd of -- of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I would ask that the witness please be shown 65 ter number D322, that is, DD -- ERN number DD001526 -- sorry, in Bosnian -- okay. I'm told DD001513.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: What is the ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: DD --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The 65 ter number, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: DD322, and it's to be MFI256.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what I'm going to show you now is a document that purports to be a telephone transcript dated the 2nd of July, 1993 between Rasim Delic and Sefer Halilovic. I would ask you just, please, when that appears in front of you to take your time to read through it, and then I'm going to ask you some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask that the Bosnian version be moved over to page 2, because on the transcript provided to us there's an irrelevant conversation on the first page. On the English version, it just takes up one paragraph, but in the Bosnian version it takes up the first page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'm sorry, Witness F, you might have been shown a -- a different -- a conversation. When you've reached the end of your page and you need to turn over the page, you indicate, please, and -- and that will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We can go on. The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the page please be turned over for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. In due course, could the English version also be turned over so that the Tribunal and Prosecutor can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could it perhaps be released so that we could look at it ourselves. At the moment, we don't have access to the document except as -- through the registry's control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. That -- sorry, I presumed that had been done. I'm sorry. I'm told it has been released, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the following page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page is not coming up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, could I just inquire: Do you have that page now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll have to be guided by Your Honours as to when you wish to turn over the page for your own purposes. I've got a hard copy myself here that I'm working with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page, please. The next page, please. The next one. The next one. The next.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: While the witness is reading, can I indicate to the Court -- the Tribunal that the -- the Bosnian version is handwritten and it's approximately 13 pages of text. Can I also indicate for timing purposes that there's one other document that I'll show him that's much -- much shorter than that, but we won't be spending the day putting the witness through this exercise apart from on this occasion and one other.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go on, please. The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the next page of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page, please. The next one. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness F, this is a document provided to the Defence by the Prosecutor at an earlier stage in these proceedings. And my first question to you is: Have you ever seen this actual document itself before today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And just to be very complete about it, did you ever hear any tape recording containing this conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On the face of the transcript, does it appear to be a document which originated in the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I saw that it was from the State Security Service. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, since you didn't see it or hear it, I'm going to ask you a second round of questions. Did you -- did you know that there were operative measures, including telephone tapping, being undertaken in respect of Sefer Halilovic by State Security Services?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I've never heard that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the meetings that you've mentioned, the internal meetings of the SVB that you attended, was it ever disclosed in those meetings that Sefer Halilovic was or might be under such telephone-tapping measures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, a correction. I never took part in any SDB meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only attended briefings --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Just stop there. I'm sorry. That must have been a -- a mistake of communication. I -- it's not being suggested that you did. I meant the SVB meetings that you attended. And now, sorry, please proceed with your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: SVB, yes, that's fine. And I also attended daily morning meetings and briefings. Nobody ever mentioned that Sefer Halilovic was under any measures of the security services.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, in those circumstances, I do not seek to tender this -- this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions though concerning the events at that time. Was it within your -- I understand you -- you knew what you were told at the meetings. And what I want to ask you is: Was it within your knowledge that Senad Pecar -- Senad Pecar was in fact a person involved in the bad activities of the 10th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know Senad Pecar at all. I don't even know him nowadays. His name was never mentioned in my presence. All I know is that Musan Topalovic was removed from the commanding post of that brigade, and after that happened, I think that the other person was appointed either Chief of Staff or -- appointed to one of the senior commanding posts. However, I repeat that I have never seen him and I do not know him at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm just confused a little bit by your answer. When you say Musan Topalovic was removed, are you now referring to the time of the Operation Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "removed," can you just explain what you mean by "removed." What happened to Musan Topalovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he was replaced. That means that he was no longer brigade commander. There probably was a decision of the commander or the president. I don't know exactly the process based on which the brigade commanders were replaced. As far as I know, Caco was killed in the Trebevic operation. I don't know the precise circumstances, because I was not kept abreast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. I have one other transcript that's been provided, but I don't want to show you that unless -- well, I'll ask you some questions first of all. Did you see any -- apart from the one that you've just indicated, did you see any other transcripts purporting to be records of telephone intercepts relevant to the events of the 2nd of July at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see. The rule is in the security service that the person who is not involved in certain topics does not receive firsthand information about that topic; therefore, I didn't see that information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in that event, I'm not going to seek to show you any other transcript. Very well. You mentioned that -- just excuse me a moment. Sorry. Pardon me one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. I just have a very short number of questions now about the time before Neretva 93 and the events in Herzegovina. You've given evidence already about the 9th and 10th Brigades being outside the line of control and command. I just want to show you an order that was issued and ask -- ask for you to comment on it. It may be that you've seen it; it may be you didn't. But I'll ask for your comment in either event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Defence 65 ter number 218. And it ERN number is DD001105, and it will be MFI257.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, this is an order which I'm just going to ask you to look at. It appears to be an order from Commander Karavelic of the 1st Corps dated the 6th of September, 1993 and directed to a 1st Corps forward command post and also to the 10th Brigade, Musan Topalovic, and Senad Pecar. Do you have that order in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, would you just have a look at that order, please, and I'll ask you some formal questions about it first and then I'll ask you for -- whether you saw it and what your opinion about it is. Now first of all, does that appear to be an order in a regular form from the commander of the 1st Corps, Vehbija Karic, directed to the forward command post of the -- of the 1st Corps and also to the commander of the 10th Mountain Brigade, Musan Topalovic and Senad Pecar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to tell you right away that the documents of the command of the 1st Corps reached me very seldom, basically never, especially not outside of the security services structure. I mostly had documents of operative nature in my hands within the scope of tasks of the security services. As for this document, yes, it does have some shortcomings, but it was possible -- it is possible that this document was issued during the wartime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness F, you've been very clear about the circumstances in which you would normally see documents and get information, but the reason I ask you about this one is because on any view your service had an interest in the movements of the 10th Brigade in the weeks leading up to this period of time and, obviously, afterwards as well. So I want to ask you: Did you become aware yourself of this particular order; namely, an order by Vahid Karavelic to a unit of the 10th Brigade to move back from Igman, where it was no longer needed, back into the city? Were you aware of such an order made by Karavelic that had consequences for where particular units of the 10th Brigade might be found early in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you: I have never seen this document and I was not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you comment on whether or not it was discussed at your SVB meetings that a unit of the 10th Brigade was being moved by Vahid Karavelic at around this time from Igman back to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember that event. The war was going on. There were numerous fightings going on in that area. And in addition to that, I in fact never followed combat activities, and I stated so yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Your Honours, I offer that document for tender. I note what the -- what the witness has said about it, that he didn't see it and he doesn't know about it. And it may be appropriate to tender it through Mr. Karavelic when he comes as well. But because I've asked the questions, I will offer it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, yes. The witness, as Mr. Morrissey has rightly pointed out, doesn't know anything about the document nor its contents and Mr. Karavelic is coming. That would be the appropriate time to tender it. Although, as it has been commented upon, it would be appropriate to mark it for identification at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. This document is not admitted into evidence through this witness without prejudice for the future tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. I agree with that -- that course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I wish to move now to events at a later stage in the investigation. If you'd just excuse me a moment. There are now a series of documents that I am going to have shown to you for comment by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown -- it's Defence 65 ter number 484. Its ERN number is DD002216. And it is to be MFI258.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a document which appears to emanate from the 1st Corps security service but which may have passed through your service, and I'm asking you to -- to look at it quickly for your comment. It appears to contain or it says it contains operative work: "Through operative work, we've obtained the following information." Would you just mind looking through it firstly and seeing whether you can indicate -- have you ever seen it before, this document? Could I just indicate: You feel free to read the whole thing if you need to. But the parts that interest me and that I want to question you about are the first paragraph where it says: "On the 2nd of October, an assault was formed as part of the 10th Brigade under the direct command of Musan Topalovic, Caco. The president of the state indirectly asked for this unit to be formed by asking Caco to provide in-depth security for his visit to Mostar." So I'll ask you about that. And then -- and then the tenth paragraph, although they're not numbered, it's the tenth one, where it says: "It is let known among the soldiers that this unit is under the direct supervision of the president of the republic and that he fully supports them in whatever they do, that this unit has his full confidence, as well as that the unit is under Alija Izetbegovic's personal command." Now, can I ask you, first of all: Have you seen this particular document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Does it appear to be the sort of document that one would expect in the normal course of events to pass through your service and be in the hands of your superiors for the purposes of the morning meetings that were held in your service?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's an objection to this line of questioning. My learned friend is showing the witness a number of documents which he clearly hasn't seen before and can't comment upon. And I object to further questioning on this line unless my friend can demonstrate some relevance to the proceedings here. He's entitled to tender the document at some point, but not necessarily through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that there more just asked a very general question on that, which is allowed. We'll see, you know, how far he could go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, well, Your Honours, I'm trying to be fairly careful about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as this document goes, I understand you say you haven't seen it personally. On the face of it, is it the sort of document that in the normal course of events should pass through the hands of your service and your superiors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document must have passed through the hands of my superiors. It's addressed to the military security service administration, and you can see that the chief of the administration initialled it and acted upon it. However, I did not hold it in my hands and I have not seen it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, at -- at the meetings which you've referred to, the SVB meetings, did you become advised of the -- the matters that I've highlighted for you there, in particular that Musan Topalovic's unit had formed a new assault unit and that this unit was rumoured to be - and I'm only using the word "rumoured" of course because that's what in the document - is this unit was rumoured to be under the direct supervision of the president of the republic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to its establishment structure, the 10th Mountain Brigade, as far as I know and to the best of my knowledge, had, I think, three battalions which were combat battalions holding the lines in the regular way. Apart from that, there was an assault company and its strength was probably about 100 men, according to our estimation, because we were not familiar with the composition of that company or its size and its manpower level. It could not have been under any kind of command, direct or otherwise, of the president of the republic. I don't think this can hold water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm certainly not asking you to say that it's proper and according to the rules. What I'm really asking you about is: Did you become aware through those meetings that this rumour or this story was circulating as operative information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I wasn't aware of that. Nobody ever mentioned anything like that. And the name of the president in connection with this assault company -- well, it was never linked to it, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'd ask that you have a chance to look at another document here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could the witness please be shown document -- Defence 65 ter number D486.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps that last document could be marked for identification, given that the -- I anticipate my learned friend won't try to tender it through this document [sic] as he's moved on. Perhaps it could be marked as the witness has commented on its contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: One moment, please. Your Honours, I'm proposing to come back to that document after this one. So I wonder if we could just hold that in abeyance for a moment. It has, in fact, in any event been ascribed a number, which is 258. But I was very likely to come back to it after this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, with respect to this document that we're about to show the witness, we should move into the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do we have the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we go back to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness please be shown document D -- Defence 65 ter number D18, which is DD000058, and it's to be MFI260.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document that I'm about to show you, it will come on the screen in just a moment. Now, this is an order signed and stamped by the chief of the SVK, Sefer Halilovic. Do you see his signature and stamp at the bottom of the -- of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do see it

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Would you just look to the top left and notice that the date of this document is 25 October 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And there's no doubt in the world that by the time of 25 October 1993 the planning for Operation Trebevic was well and truly in process; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I just want to take you through this document here and confirm a couple of matters, bearing in mind the interest shown by your service in Mr. Halilovic's opinions and expressions. Do you see here where Mr. Halilovic says -- and I'll go to the second -- go to the first paragraph -- "At our last joint meeting, it was agreed that talks should be conducted with commanders of the 9th, 10th, 1st, and 2nd Mountain Brigades about setting aside some forces and sending them to the front in Herzegovina. Talks were conducted with the commanders of the 1st and 2nd Mountain Brigades and they are prepared to set aside some forces, but they're concerned about a possible clash with the 9th and the 10th Mountain Brigades, which left a bad impression on the team that I'm [inaudible], and led us to conclude they that will be able to set aside some forces if some forces are taken from the 9th and 10th Brigades." New paragraph: "Since despite our best efforts we were unable to contact Musan Topalovic, also known as Caco, commander of the 10th Mountain Brigade, and only briefly talked with the commander of the 9th Mountain Brigade, with whom we did not manage to agree on anything, I propose a meeting through the chain of command and control (since I do not have the right to issue orders) of the commanders of the 1st, 2nd, 9th, and 10th Mountain Brigades and the commander of the 2nd Independent Battalion in one of your offices on 25 October 1993 at 1900 hours or some other time that suits you better in order to agree on how to carry out the upcoming task and where you could issue the necessary orders." New paragraph: "We have unsuccessfully tried to organise such a meeting three days in a row. But since we were unable to achieve anything, we are forced to contact you in this way." And then it indicates that it's forwarded to the commander of the SVK, the commander of the 1st Corps, and to files. Now, my first question is this: In the preparations for Trebevic and in particular the very day before it happened, this document must have passed through the hands of your service. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't be precise in my answer. The document is not addressed at all or sent to the military security service administration. It could have reached the chief of the administration, my superior, but it did not reach me, so I can say nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can say something about it. And I'll -- I'll ask you some further questions. I agree it's not addressed to your service at all. It's addressed to Rasim Delic and Vahid Karavelic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But one person who was not included in the planning for Operation Trebevic and in particular for the arrests was Sefer Halilovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Halilovic was not one of the people planning his own arrest on the 26th of October; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that. I don't know that Halilovic was arrested on the 26th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I -- I accept your correction about that. But you certainly agree that he was not involved in the planning of the arrest of the -- those people who you processed from the 9th and 10th Brigades; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I think he was not involved, but I don't know to what extent he was aware of it. This was above my level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I understand. But the question is -- my questions go a bit further than that. Were you aware at the time that the 10th Brigade -- sorry, were you aware at the time that Sefer Halilovic was being deceived as part of the planning for Trebevic into thinking that there was a need to go back to Herzegovina with units from the 1st, 2nd, 9th, and 10th Brigades? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of it at all and I don't know how he was deceived. I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's just that on the face of this document here it appears that Halilovic is talking to Rasim Delic about an upcoming operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's an objection to this continuing line of question on a document the witness hasn't seen before, doesn't know whether it went to his service, and knows nothing about the contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'll deal with the matter a different way, but I offer this document for tender in any event as one signed by Halilovic and it's not -- well, I agree that -- this witness, I've got some more questions for, but I'm offering it for tender at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Subject to the Defence establishing its provenance, the Prosecution doesn't object to it being tendered on that basis, that it is a document purportedly signed by the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'll make that inquiry and subject to that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- of course, being satisfied, I offer it on that basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I should ask you this question formally, although it was implicit in your answer earlier: Have you ever seen this document before today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware -- leaving aside this document itself, were you aware --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just excuse me a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Were you aware of whether or not there was a plan or a suggestion for an ongoing operation in Herzegovina at the time of the 25th and 26th of October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of it. I knew about the earlier operation on the territory of Herzegovina when the well-known crime was committed. I didn't know about this operation. Our intentions were to carry out the Trebevic operation. That's what we were focussing on in the security service administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the fact, isn't it, that Commander Delic had personal control over Operation Trebevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I would seek -- very well. Well, I offer that document for tender. Can I indicate that the chain of custody or my instructions is that this document was obtained from the archives of the Army of Bosnia in Sarajevo by one of our investigators, Mr. Asim Dzambasovic. He's present in court. He can be asked questions about that if needs be. But that's the provenance of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to show you now another document. This is Defence 65 ter number D27. It's DD002777 [Realtime transcript read in error "DD00002777"] and will be MFI261. Witness F, the -- the document that's going to come up now seems to be a draft -- either a draft or an official version of the plan for Trebevic. And I just want to show it to you and see whether you've seen it before and whether it accurately captures what you understood to be the purpose of the operation and the details of the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: May I indicate for the Prosecutor's benefit and also for the Court's that this is a document which has an annex attached to it which is included. I wasn't going to take the witness to it, but it's part of the document, so we -- it's -- it's included in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that document on your screen as yet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just give us a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I indicate for the benefit of the witness and the Court that there are three to four further documents to go, and that will essentially complete the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think there may have been too many digits read out by my learned friend. There's four "0"s there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There should be only two. The number is DD002777. Or "triple seven," as previously described.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, my legal assistant has identified a technical problem. It appears that the second page of the Bosnian version has not been successfully scanned. In order to solve it -- it's okay in English, but the witness needs to have it in the proper language. In order for that to be rectified, he's going to go and photocopy a hard copy and present that and we'll make good, of course, the difficulty. But rather than delay, I can move to a different document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, I apologise for that. We've just had a technical problem about that document. I be ask you about that in a moment, but I'll just take you to a different document in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, we're going to see how we can cope without Mr. Cengic's assistance. Could the witness please be shown document -- it's Defence 65 ter number D150. The number -- ERN number is DD000671. I think this is to be MFI262.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document that we're going to attempt to bring up on the screen now, Witness F, is a bulletin -- sorry, an SVB bulletin dated 19 September 1993. And I'm just going to ask you to look at that document. Now, do you have that on the screen in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is that in the regular form of a -- of a weekly bulletin which was produced by your service as a regular and repetitive part of its work in that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Could the witness please be shown the following page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, as you're looking at it -- you feel free to read whatever parts you want. I'm going to take you to the first paragraph and the last -- and two of the last three paragraphs. But, of course, if you need to familiarise yourself with the rest of it, do not hesitate to do so. Now, do you have in front of you the -- the paragraph commencing with the sentence: "Following the recent incident between members of the 2nd Brigade and the 10th Brigade, Musan Topalovic called Zakir Puskar and Mujo Zulic and suggested they join him in his intention to form a new Bosnian army, stating that he did not recognise the 1st Corps or any authority in the city and suggesting they take power jointly." Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see the part that comes after that, that: "Caco would engage Serbian and Croatian soldiers and former JNA people's army officers in the new army solely in work platoons and they would not be armed. Only Muslims would have the right to bear arms"? Do you see that -- that passage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say that Puskar and Zulic rejected his proposals, after which Caco threatened to attack their staffs. Because of this -- and it goes on to describe other matters. And then the last sentence: "Members of the 1st and 2nd Brigade commands believe the attack on them and probably the attempt to take power in the city will occur following the return to Sarajevo of Ramiz Delalic, also known as Celo, because he shares Topalovic's opinions." Now, my first question is: Was that operative information that passed through your organisation now while you were working there on the 19th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's quite logical that it did, because the service compiled this bulletin. I was a member of the service. So obviously yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a little bit hard to ask you to remember every single rumour that came through your service, I appreciate, but do you recall this one, in your own memory, and leaving aside this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall the document. I think in the left bottom corner I saw a number, 180 or something --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- which means there were many such bulletins and I cannot recall. The service compiled these, and they were also used to inform people externally, people outside the service, that is, the army commander, probably the MUP, and the political structures. This information contained in the bulletins had to be checked. I'm deeply convinced of that. And they had to be of a high degree of reliability. I cannot recall these details. I didn't have these bulletins in my hands. I was informed of their contents at the morning briefings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But this document -- I understand you say you can't recall this specific one, and you're quite right. It's -- it's got number 188 on it, so they were very frequent. But I understand you say you can't recall this particular document, but nevertheless this information was obviously available to you in the course of your work at the time; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not necessarily -- I wasn't necessarily informed of all the details. It would depend on the assessment of the chief of the security service administration. It was his practice if he assessed that he had to inform the people from the administration or the lower units with the contents of a bulletin, he would write it down on the document and initial it. He would say: "Inform everyone," or "inform the following," and then a list of names. And I did not see this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Very well. But just to get you to comment nevertheless on the rumours which were -- which were circulating at the time. The rumour that Caco would engage Serbian Croatian soldiers and former JNA officers in the work platoons, do you recall that particular rumour circulating? Perhaps I should ask you this: Were you a JNA officer yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I was not a JNA officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Sefer Halilovic a JNA officer or had he been a JNA officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met Sefer Halilovic on the 8th of April, 1992, I think, which is when he passed over into our army. I heard that he left the JNA very early on, and I think he had been a major in the JNA and that he joined the patriotic forces for the defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina very early on and for this reason he was very popular among the citizens, and I personally liked him very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just have a couple of other questions. This document here has got a mark on it at -- on the front page "Strictly confidential." And I wanted to ask you whether that means it was -- it was a report that was denied to you or whether it was a report that could be accessed by you, if you felt the need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown the first page of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You see the -- the "Strictly confidential" stamp. Who does that mean it's confidential from? Was it confidential from you, for example, or was it confidential from people outside of the SVB organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can't say it was confidential from me personally. As I have just said, the chief of the security service administration evaluated at what level and what persons had to be informed of the contents of the bulletin. For example, it's possible in a certain situation for information I had verified to be included in the bulletin, and the information gathered from various operations officers and people from the service, these were compiled and collated and put in the bulletin. They were not to be copied or made public or leave the service except for certain people who regularly received the bulletin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, just so that we're quite clear about this. You don't have any recollection of seeing this particular document yourself; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I have never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, it appears to you to be a document in -- in a very common format which circulated to some extent within your service, the service of the SVB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Well, then I'll ask you comments on it strictly in a professional capacity and bearing in mind that you do not -- that you didn't see it or you don't recall seeing it. Would you look, please, to the -- the last three paragraphs. I won't ask you to go through these in detail, but I just want you to note the details of bad behaviour by various units. If you need the page to be turned over, please indicate, because the court staff will help you. And I can indicate in advance what my question is going to be, so while you're reading it you can think of it, that -- the question is: Is it the case that units other than the 9th and 10th Brigades did from time to time have individuals who committed wrongful acts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember, but it's quite possible. There was a large number of men. There were many brigades. However, such information did not come to me because, as I said both yesterday and today, I had no connections with the combat activities of various brigades. I was involved with the work of the staff of the main command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, not on the basis that it's a document emanating from the service and it's a standard document. I have one concern about a portion of the document, and that is can it be -- can the second page not be broadcast publicly but just be shown to the Trial Chamber, the third paragraph or the third bullet point, which starts: "We are in possession of indicators that" a named person, et cetera, "is collaborating with the aggressor." Having never seen this document before, obviously it's just come up at the moment, I -- the Prosecution has concerned that if that particular piece of information were publicly released or broadcast or not redacted from the exhibit, it could well endanger the person named there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd have no objection to that entire paragraph being redacted, if that -- frankly, the Prosecution have a -- a better perspective on security matters at large than -- than I do. And if my friend identifies a possible problem, that paragraph is immaterial to what this witness is being asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This document is admitted into the evidence with the redaction agreed by both parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, I now believe that we're in a position to show you the plan for Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown MFI262 -- sorry, 261. 261, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect to this document, this is the one we tried to show before. What we'll do is circulate copies of the -- the Bosnian original but because of the difficulties that were encountered last week that Your Honour may recall, where we gave the Prosecutor an original document and then later on it turned out that we hadn't given them the -- the new translation, we'll also provide the English translation as well in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's going to be provided now is -- is a document provided to the Defence which seems to be a plan for Trebevic. And we'd just ask you to look at it and see what -- see whether you've seen it before and what your comment about it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. May I see page 2 of the previous document, because I didn't have it on my screen and you said it would be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we're going to give you both page 1 and page 2 in paper.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've already given my reply, but I haven't seen what the document is about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They're just going to bring it now. Yes. Sorry, now can I just ask: Do you have that paper document in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've received a new document, not the second page of the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just want to clarify this, Your Honour. Would you excuse me, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just confirm what you have. Do you have in front of you a document dated 25th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And is it numbered 1/297-492?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And now --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I just indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before my friend goes on, if it speeds proceedings up, we don't object to the tendering of this document, whether or not the witness has seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, but I'll still take the witness through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Okay. Now, is this the order from Rasim Delic to form the relevant groups to conduct Operation Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a copy of the document. However, I can see that this is his order, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You see that there are two teams -- or sorry, two groups being referred to, one being, if you like, the command group and the other being a group consisting of members to direct the operation. So far as you performed functions in Trebevic, under which of those two categories did you fall into in. Were you in the Alispahic-Karavelic-Jasarevic group, or were you in the command group with Ismet Dahic and others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean Ismet Dahic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I -- that's what I meant to say. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time, I was a member of the military security administration and it was logical for me to be in a group which was represented by Jusuf Jasarevic, who was in the command group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The reason I asked you is because Vahid Bogunic appears in the other group and he was also a member of your command.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I -- Your Honours, I tender that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Since there's no objections from the Prosecution, it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a final reference to that document. This is a document -- although this document is dated the 25th of October, the planning had been going on for quite some time before that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most likely, yes. We started planning the action somewhat earlier, because it wasn't possible to do it in just one day, so we started with preparations earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a -- can you provide the Tribunal with a date on which this preparation started, or is that not possible to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the final two documents I have to ask you about relate to 1995 and 1996 -- oh, sorry, no, there's one other one before that. One short one before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Defence 65 ter number D115. This is DD000473 and this will be MFI263.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, you may have seen before; you may not have seen. In any event, I'll ask you to comment upon it. But it's the order of the Presidency formally removing Sefer Halilovic as Chief of Staff of the army. So I'm going to show it to you and then -- and then ask you to comment on it. It's dated 1st of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: 263, Your Honour. Did say -- pardon me. I apologise if I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. I just want to make sure. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, it is 263.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have in front of you an order from Alija Izetbegovic relieving Sefer Halilovic from the duty of the Chief of the Main Staff, such order to take effect immediately and dated 1st of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, there's no objection. I think that's actually on the Prosecution 65 ter list as well. I'm just getting the case manager to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is it admitted into evidence before?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm just -- I'm just checking. It's happened very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't believe it has been admitted in. It's likely to be somewhere on the Prosecution's 65 ter list, I'd agree. I think it hasn't been; hence, I'm putting it through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So this document is admitted into the evidence. And once it is admitted into the evidence, I believe there's no clear distinction between which document it is. I mean, whether it has been tendered by the Prosecution or by the Defence. There's no difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, there is a -- a habit of labeling the documents with a "P" or a "D" before them, but that has no effect on the way in which the Tribunal uses the document in due course. Yes, okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the final two questions relate to events much later, in 1995 and 1996, and there are document which I want to show you in regard to that and ask for your comment on them and ask whether you've seen them as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown -- it's Defence 65 ter number D31, three-one, and its ERN number is DD002788, and it will be MFI 264.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document I'm about to show you is an official note of the SVB, and it's dated 30th of November, 1995. Do you have that document in front of you as yet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I would like you to be shown the final page of that document. I'm going to give you a chance to look through it in just a moment, but I'd like you to be -- be shown the final page of that document for a moment. Do you have that, the final page, including the final signature -- sorry, including the -- a final section entitled "Measures proposed"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's -- it's been indicated to me that this should be done in private session, so I'd seek that we go into the private session for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. Pardon me. I was just waiting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you see here that generally speaking the document constitutes an analysis by Damir Dzanko of Sefer Halilovic's newspaper article and then after that the person you've indicated has proposed certain measures, and the particular -- well, sorry, yes, first of all: Do you understand that to be the effect of this document, that it's a document drawn up by Dzanko and then proposals have been placed at the end of that document by your colleague?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution objects to questioning in relation to this document. The date of the document appears to be the 30th of November, 1995, which is some two years after the indictment period. The Prosecution fails to see the -- the relevance of this document or -- or questions in relation to what the security service may have done in relation to Mr. Halilovic's article some years later. Mr. Halilovic writing the article may be relevant to the proceedings, but not the response of the security service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since that article is relevant to this case and this document is closely related to this article, so the question is allowed in this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you explain to the Tribunal, please, what is "KOZ," which is referred to in the third and fourth points of the measures proposed. What is "KOZ"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "KOZ" is on abbreviation for "counter-intelligence protection," so it means in this case the counter-intelligence protection of the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any rule that you're aware of that permits KOZ measures to include making media attacks on Sefer Halilovic by third persons on the basis of other matters or other topics altogether in order to protect the commander of the Bosnian army? In other words, do you know of a rule that allows that sort of behaviour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to attempt to explain this. The counter-intelligence protection as a measure of the security service is of defensive nature. Its aim is to protect, to defend. At that time, and speaking about Sefer Halilovic, in light of this official note, let me tell you that Sefer Halilovic was not a member of the army at the time, as far as I know. Therefore, there was no need to undertake any measures with respect to him, based on the rules and all legislation and regulations, he was outside of the competence of the military security service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the basis for recommending there should be a media attack mounted on Sefer Halilovic by a third person in relation to a third topic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not aware of that; therefore, I cannot give you any comments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you can give a professional comment on whether it's legal to do that or not. And what I'm asking you to do is identify the legal basis for conducting this particular activity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my previous answer, I attempted to explain. The counter-intelligence protection is a measure used by the military security service, was used in accordance with our rules and methodology. The commander of the army had a right -- or rather, the service was duty-bound to protect the commander of the army by using counter-intelligence protection to protect him in his place of residence, place of work, and any of -- any movements that he had. I have never heard of any counter-intelligence protection in relation to this person; therefore, I cannot comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when -- sorry, I'll take a step back from that. What you say is that you had -- you personally had no involvement in any such measures against Sefer Halilovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it ever discussed at an official meeting of your organisation that Sefer Halilovic should be the subject of a smear campaign in the press?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never. And I can assure you of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because it's quite plain, isn't it, that from the army commander's point of view Halilovic's allegations were that Commander Delic was aware of all of the -- sorry, I'm just going to put a part of this to you. It was part of -- of Halilovic's allegation here, as you understand it, or as you understood it at the time, I should say, that Halilovic was alleging that Delic should have taken steps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, well, I'll put the question in a different way and I'll read a quote from the thing. Damir Dzanko summarises Sefer's position as being: "Sefer further states that the option of covering up the responsibility of those actually responsible for the dishonourable acts in the village of Grabovica prevailed, which means -- which meant that he had to be indirectly accused of carrying out those acts. Sefer says that he is certain that the competent organs know who is responsible for what and their names but some invisible hand wants the culprits never to be discovered." Now, I'm not asking you about the truth or otherwise of these matters. I understand that's not within your area. But you understand that was the allegation that Damir Dzanko was concerned about in this letter; in other words, the allegation made by Halilovic that there were some people who didn't want the truth to come out about Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once again, I do not understand the question. What do you want to ask me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll put the question another way. It's the -- look at the last paragraph and I'll ask you about that, the last paragraph being Damir Dzanko's last paragraph: "I believe that that open letter by Sefer Halilovic represents an attack on the Chief of the General Staff of the Bosnian army and that by choosing this manner of addressing the public Halilovic attempts to prevent any accusations of war crimes that have been committed. It's to be expected that Halilovic will use this interview for his propaganda activities." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I understand your position is you did not become involved in -- in this matter in 1995 and 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But it's also obvious to you, isn't it, that this document represents an attempt -- or sorry, represents a measure designed to protect Rasim Delic from the allegations of Sefer Halilovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The way I see it, this is just an opinion of one agent, who made a conclusion based on the information stated above. Therefore, this is his opinion and it is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you just excuse me for one moment, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I've nearly finished. And there's one matter that -- I want to take one second, if I could, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But we have to stop here to take a break. So we'll have a break and we'll resume at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, as usual, having a break shortens the questions that are coming afterwards. And I've now finished the questioning and there is just one other matter that I need to raise. The witness was inadvertently misled by the Defence earlier on because he had a document that was a faulty document put in his hands, and in fact the document -- the witness himself identified this when he said that he'd like to see the second page, which he hadn't seen. At the time, I thought he was talking about something else. The document in question, it's MFI262. Now, what I had in mind -- I mentioned this to the learned Prosecutor on the break. And I had in mind to briefly show the witness the full document. The actual page that was missing is not part of the Defence case, and I take it not part of the Prosecution case either, and it also contains that name that my learned friend wanted to have suppressed. So it's technically in a sense irrelevant. But because the witness raised it, it should in fairness to him -- that he should have the chance to look at that. So I just ask to show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you could have that hard copy shown to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just indicate that because of printing reasons, it's -- it's double-sided. And that's the reason why the scanning error took place, in fact, that it was a double-sided matter. So we apologise to the witness, frankly, because he's the one who noticed the problem. But if we could just show that to him. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness F. You've heard what I've just said there. You made an inquiry about a document. It may not be relevant, but in any event, we're going to show you and allow you to notice it and make any comment, if you do have a comment to make about it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: What document is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This is MFI262. And could I just indicate that the English-language version is complete, but the witness was denied the full document. We will, of course, provide the fully scanned version as soon as today's session is finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, did you have an opportunity to briefly read that page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am just reading it now, and I can see that the contents of this document are new to me. I asked to see it earlier because I didn't see it on the screen. That was the only reason why I asked for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I understand that. And I'm grateful to you for taking the time to look at it. But the fact is it doesn't change your memory about the rest of the document; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, those are my questions. And thank you for your patience in answering them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There will be on one issue. But I think there's two documents outstanding. I think there's one document outstanding from the cross-examination. It was D2216, which I don't think got an MFI number at the time. Was it 258? I'm not sure it's been admitted into evidence. I'm not sure whether my learned friend was proposing to tender it. I thought he was at the time but if he's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, he was intending and we are waiting for your response. Do you agree or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, I don't. The -- my response is: If my learned friend can demonstrate the relevance of that particular document to the proceedings, the Prosecution will withdraw its objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, pardon me, Your Honour. Sorry. I -- I just had become used to the practice of doing this at the end, but I'm happy to do it now, if needs be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: With respect to this -- this particular document, this is a document which this witness did not himself see on his account. Your Honours will recall that he was cross-examined about the substance of -- sorry, about the information that was contained in it and concerning a link between the president of the state and the assault unit of the 10th Brigade, Musan Topalovic. It was cross-examined upon. It may be relevant to the way in which you deal with -- sorry, perhaps the answers he gave in respect to the later document may reflect upon his knowledge of these matters. It's a document that circulated, that was in the SVB sector, if you like. If it came from the -- from the MUP or the SVB, I wouldn't be seeking to tender it because it's outside of his organisation. This -- although he -- he clearly has said and has steadfastly said it's not his document, he didn't see it; nevertheless, it's from -- it's from within his organisation. He can offer comments upon it. And although, like -- quite frankly, like a lot of the evidence given in good faith, no doubt, given here it's relatively remote sort of evidence. Nevertheless, it may have some evidence to the case. It could bear upon questions of effective control and the like.
